critique: The render retains a bright orange/yellow fire palette, but it is still a compact explosion: t1 is an overexposed white-hot orb and by t4 it ejects a wide, evenly radial field of crisp ember dots. This is opposite the thumbnail intent of soft, layered smoke-and-fire haze with a coherent rising plume. There is almost no lingering volume, the fire core clips to white, and the t1-to-t4 motion disperses too rapidly rather than billowing upward.

suggestions.why: Greatly reduce particle travel so emitted material remains as a dense lingering haze instead of expanding into a large spark burst by t4.
Narrow the directional cone to suppress the symmetric radial scatter and establish a unified plume.
Rotate the directional emission upward so the slowed particles build a fire-and-smoke column rather than an outward blast.
Use larger sprite particles to create overlapping soft volume rather than individually legible ember circles.
Replace additive accumulation with the less clipping blend mode so the central flame resolves into orange/red layers instead of a white saturated disk.
